title: The Hatha Yoga Pradipika
attributionNote: The treatise is ascribed to Svātmārāma, a disciple of Gorakṣanātha. Little is known of the author, and the text draws on earlier Nath and Siddha traditions.
description: The Hatha Yoga Pradipika is the classic manual of hatha yoga in four chapters: the postures and the place and manner of practice; breath control and the purification of the channels; the seals and locks that raise the vital breath; and the states of absorption that lead to liberation. It is the source of much of the posture and breath practice now taught worldwide.
historicalContext: Svātmārāma compiled the Pradipika in the fifteenth century from earlier Yoga Upanishads and Nath works. Pancham Sinh's English translation, published in 1914, is the first complete rendering and remains a standard public-domain edition; it is a literal translation with the author's own explanatory notes.
availabilityNote: Complete. All four chapters of Pancham Sinh's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The volume's introduction and table of contents are not part of the work.
